Accessibility disclosure

Justnoise uses Android Accessibility only while you have explicitly enabled its app-blocking service. It reads window-change event types and the foreground app identifier to compare with the apps you selected. Only the latest app identifier is kept temporarily in service memory; it is cleared when the screen turns off or the service is interrupted or disconnected. It does not read screen content, typed text, passwords, notifications, or accessibility nodes, and does not save a foreground-app history. Nothing is sent off this device. Your selected apps, consent, session state and keyed Zap digest stay in private local storage. For schedules, you choose automatic start times; tap your Zap to stop. Schedule settings, replay-prevention markers and the latest outcome stay local until that schedule is deleted, you withdraw, clear storage, or uninstall. Android exact-alarm access is requested separately when you enable schedules. Delivery can be delayed or missed; Force Stop requires explicit app recovery and never catches up old starts. For History, the app saves a random session ID, start/end times, duration, selected-app count and whether the session was interrupted. History contains no app names or event log. Session time does not prove continuous blocking. History stays local until withdrawal, clearing storage or uninstall. You can withdraw below, disable Accessibility, Force Stop, or uninstall at any time.
I understand this disclosure and choose to enable Justnoise app blocking with Accessibility.
